propositions: The statement explains changes in cash and cash equivalents and classifies cash flows as operating, investing and financing.
Direct and indirect methods are alternative presentations of operating cash flows; direct method reports major gross receipts/payments, indirect method adjusts profit or loss.
IAS 7 encourages the direct method; the lecture's almost-all wording is not a current universal usage statistic.

Investing cash flows cover long-term assets and investments outside cash equivalents, subject to dealing/trading scope; investing and financing gross receipts/payments are not changed by the CFO presentation method.

official_external_sources.effective_date: Annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027; earlier application permitted.
propositions: The indirect-method starting point changes to operating profit or loss.
For entities without specified main business activities, interest received and dividends received are investing; interest paid and dividends paid are financing.
Entities with specified main business activities apply the amended single-category requirements for the relevant items.
